risks.description: The exception detail screen is built from a ReviewPayload that snapshots WorkflowState at build time, while the packet page re-reads live state via store.get_run. If these paths ever diverge (payload rendered, then the run transitions APPROVED/DISPUTED/DONE), the operator can see a state the backend no longer holds and act on a stale next-action.
risks.basis: AC 'the screen never shows a state the backend does not currently hold' (weight 3); review.py build_review_payload gates on run.state==NEEDS_REVIEW and stores state as a snapshot, packet_page.py line 51 reads live run.

risks.description: A signed action generated from a stale screen must not apply after the run's state has moved; otherwise the screen effectively drove an action against a state the backend does not hold.
risks.basis: action_callback.py WorkflowError path returns 409 'The workflow state has changed, so this action was not applied.'; AC3.

risks.description: The screen may name a next action without naming who owns it, or vice versa, leaving an unowned obligation.
risks.basis: AC 'names the next action and who owns it' (weight 3); routing/operator_role and action_options in review.py.

risks.description: Evidence the exception was raised from may be omitted or unlinked, so the operator cannot see why the exception exists.
risks.basis: AC 'shows the evidence the exception was raised from' (weight 2); evidence_links in review.py / packet_page.py.

unresolved_questions: No browser and no live HTTP route in the approved surface reaches the rendered exception detail screen (the callback service at 127.0.0.1:8001 serves signed actions, not the packet/detail page, which is a statically generated file). Runtime verification of the exact DOM the operator sees is therefore not possible with the approved commands — coverage here is via unit/integration tests and backend-truth guards, not the live rendered page. A live-render or browser harness would be needed to verify the actual screen text.

No code symbol literally named 'exception detail screen' exists; I mapped it to the packet detail page (packet_page.py) built from ReviewPayload (review.py), rendering state, reasons, evidence_links, action_options and routing/operator_role. If U-UI-11 targets a different UI surface, requirement_references and the cited tests must be revised.

The three acceptance criteria are PENDING and I could not confirm the suite contains assertions that specifically bind the exception detail screen to (a) a named owner for the next action, (b) the raised-from evidence, or (c) live-vs-snapshot state equality. A green run of the pre-existing test_review.py / test_packet_page.py proves no regression but does not by itself prove the new AC behavior; if the builder added those assertions they live in these files and are exercised by scenarios 02–04. A dedicated stale-state test (build payload at state NEEDS_REVIEW, transition the run, assert the rendered page shows the new state and offers no stale action) appears to be the key missing guard for AC3.

review.py defaults operator_role to 'owner/operator' and evidence_base_url to localhost:8000 — I could not confirm whether the exception detail screen names a real accountable owner per exception or a static default role; if it is a static default, AC1's 'who owns it' may be satisfied only nominally.
